blocks.text: Maillardville Houses: streets and boundaries

items.t: Maillardville is the City of Coquitlam's oldest and most historic neighbourhood, in the city's southwest, centred on Brunette Avenue — the commercial main street the City's neighbourhood plan works to restore — with the house streets running north of Brunette Avenue toward Austin Avenue.

The French-language street names on the house streets are part of the record, not decoration: TransLink's route 153 stops on Brunette Avenue at Laval Street, Schoolhouse Street, Marmont Street, Nelson Street, Lebleu Street, Blue Mountain Street and Bernatchey Street.

blocks.text: Maillardville Houses: the housing stock

items.t: Detached houses are the historic stock here: the Maillardville Neighbourhood Plan's stated work includes conservation of heritage homes and preservation of the existing street, block and lot patterns, which is the small-lot mill-era pattern the house streets still follow.

Infill on house lots is plan-directed, not free-form: the plan encourages detached Housing Choices development in its Neighbourhood Attached Residential areas, designed to complement the historic and existing built-form character of the streets around it.

blocks.text: Maillardville Houses: rules that affect buyers

items.t: Heritage buildings on house lots are conserved through Heritage Revitalization Agreements: the Maillardville Neighbourhood Plan requires the conservation of heritage buildings through the use of Heritage Revitalization Agreements as part of redevelopment for projects with heritage buildings.

Maillardville has its own plan where Chineside and Central Coquitlam do not: the Maillardville Neighbourhood Plan, adopted as Schedule "A" to Bylaw No. 4465, 2014 and now carried in the Interim Official Community Plan's Schedule J list, guides growth and reinvestment in the neighbourhood.

blocks.text: Maillardville Houses: local details a buyer would not know

items.t: The neighbourhood elementary school is a named district school, not an anonymous catchment: Alderson Elementary, kindergarten to Grade 5, is listed by the province's school directory at 825 Gauthier Avenue, and École Maillard Middle, Grades 6 to 8, at 1300 Rochester Avenue.
The library branch for this side of Coquitlam is the Poirier Branch at 575 Poirier Street, west of the neighbourhood, not the City Centre Branch at 1169 Pinetree Way.

The Austin Heights sewer upgrade touches the neighbourhood's north edge: its final phase installs a new sewer main on Casey Street between Brunette Avenue and Cartier Avenue in summer and fall 2026, about two months, weather dependent.

Mackin Park is the neighbourhood park the plan process heard about repeatedly: open-house comments in the plan record called for improvements to Mackin Park and expanded community and leisure services in Maillardville.

blocks.text: Maillardville Houses: costs and taxes

items.t: The Maillardville-specific cost check is heritage process, not the tax rate: a redevelopment involving a heritage building proceeds through a Heritage Revitalization Agreement under the neighbourhood plan, which adds a City process a buyer of a non-heritage Coquitlam house lot does not face.

blocks.text: Maillardville Houses: getting around

items.t: Route 153 is the neighbourhood's bus: Braid Station to Coquitlam Central Station via Brunette Avenue through Maillardville, then Laurentian Crescent, Austin Avenue, Poirier Street, Foster Avenue, Linton Street and Como Lake Avenue, per TransLink's timetable effective September 7, 2026.
No SkyTrain station is in Maillardville; the route 153 endpoints, Braid Station and Coquitlam Central Station, are the two station connections for the house streets.

blocks.text: Maillardville Houses: risks and due diligence

items.t: Check the heritage status of the specific house before anything else: the plan requires conservation of heritage buildings through Heritage Revitalization Agreements on redevelopment, and the Laval Square and Allard-LeBleu Heritage Character Areas concentrate that risk on named streets.

Check creek and flood setbacks on the south-slope lots: Zoning Bylaw No. 3000, 1996 section 519 sets no building within 30 metres of the natural boundary of the Brunette, Coquitlam, Fraser or Pitt rivers, or within 15 metres of another qualifying watercourse, and no building below the flood construction level in designated floodplain.

faq.q: How many houses are for sale in Maillardville?
faq.a: At the end of October 2026 the Greater Vancouver REALTORS® figures showed 15 houses listed in Maillardville. That is a month-end count and it moves daily; ask Jared what is on the market today.

faq.q: Is Maillardville a buyers’ or sellers’ market for houses?
faq.a: In October 2026, houses in Maillardville had a sales ratio of 7%, which the reports’ scale reads as a buyers’ market. On the reports’ scale under 12% favours buyers, 12% to 20% is balanced and over 20% favours sellers.

faq.q: How many houses sold in Maillardville from June to October 2026?
faq.a: 4 houses sold in Maillardville over those 5 months, out of 273 in all of Coquitlam.

faq.q: Does this page include townhomes or duplexes in Maillardville?
faq.a: No. The figures are for detached houses only. Condos and townhomes are counted on their own page.

faq.q: Can I tear down an older Maillardville house and rebuild?
faq.a: The Maillardville Neighbourhood Plan requires heritage buildings to be conserved through Heritage Revitalization Agreements as part of redevelopment, and the plan's stated direction is conservation of heritage homes and preservation of the existing street, block and lot patterns. A teardown candidate has to be checked against the City's heritage records and the plan's two Heritage Character Areas, Laval Square and Allard-LeBleu, before its value is priced as a bare lot.

faq.q: Which elementary school is in Maillardville?
faq.a: Alderson Elementary, kindergarten to Grade 5, at 825 Gauthier Avenue, is the School District No. 43 (Coquitlam) elementary school in the neighbourhood, and École Maillard Middle, Grades 6 to 8, is at 1300 Rochester Avenue.

faq.q: What growth does the plan allow around the house streets?
faq.a: The updated Maillardville Neighbourhood Plan was developed to guide growth and reinvestment over 20 to 25 years and to accommodate an additional 6,000 residents and increased employment in the plan area. The growth is directed mainly to the high-density, mixed-use Neighbourhood Centre on Brunette Avenue, while the house streets are handled through heritage conservation, the two Heritage Character Areas and detached Housing Choices infill.

faq.q: Is there a bus through Maillardville to a SkyTrain station?
faq.a: Yes — route 153 runs through the neighbourhood on Brunette Avenue. TransLink's timetable routing takes route 153 from Braid Station via Brunette Avenue, Laurentian Crescent, Austin Avenue, Poirier Street, Foster Avenue, Linton Street and Como Lake Avenue to Coquitlam Central Station, with Brunette Avenue stops at Bernatchey Street, Blue Mountain Street, Lebleu Street, Nelson Street, Marmont Street, Laval Street and Schoolhouse Street. Both end stations are SkyTrain stations.

faq.q: What did houses in Maillardville sell for?
faq.a: 7 houses sold in Maillardville between November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026, with a median price of $1,890,000.

faq.q: How long do houses take to sell in Maillardville?
faq.a: The median was 61 days from listing to sale, and homes sold at a median 94.4% of the last list price (0% sold above list), for sales November 1, 2025 to October 22, 2026.
